review.market_summary: 1) Hawkish rates shock. October CPI came in hot at +0.4%, Fed officials are openly talking about a 50bp hike, and Goldman has changed its Fed forecast. The 10-year Treasury yield is above 5%, and yields had their biggest jump since the tariff selloff. This is the strongest, highest-volume signal (monetary policy +0.72, inflation +0.67), and it is the only theme I'm trading. 2) AI and semiconductor stress. Investigations into Nvidia's China exports have already knocked NVDA down 18% in five days. The headlines are specific to Nvidia, and most of the move has already happened, so there is little left to trade. CoreWeave's earnings 'AI revival' did not hold (CRWV is down 9%). 3) Oil and geopolitics are noise right now. The Iran–Hormuz headlines are being offset by OPEC+ output increases and a smaller war premium. The energy-supply score is near zero and XLE is down 6.7%. Overall: express the rates view through the cleanest instruments (dollar, long bonds, rate-sensitive small caps), keep sizes moderate because a single CPI print can fade and a 5% 10-year tends to attract buyers, and don't chase the chip names after their drop.
